'''Kera''' is an [[East Chadic languages|East Chadic language]] spoken by 45,000 people in Southwest [[Chad]] and 6,000 people in North [[Cameroon]].{{citation needed |date=July 2025}}

It was called "Tuburi" by [[Joseph Greenberg]], a name shared with [[Tupuri language|Tupuri]].

In Cameroon, Kera is spoken by small, isolated and scattered groups in the southern departments of [[Mayo-Danay]] ([[Wina, Cameroon|Wina]] commune) and [[Diamaré]] ([[Ndoukoula]] district) in the Far North Region. It is mainly spoken in Chad. In Cameroon, the main group is near the border, south of [[Viri]]. There are about 6,000 speakers in Cameroon.<ref name="ALCAM2012">{{cite book|editor-last=Binam Bikoi|editor-first=Charles|date=2012|title=Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM)|trans-title=Linguistic Atlas of Cameroon|volume=1: Inventaire des langues|language=fr|location=Yaoundé|publisher=CERDOTOLA|series=Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale (ALAC)|isbn=9789956796069}}</ref>

==== Labiodental flap ====
Kera has a labiodental flap {{IPAslink|ⱱ}}, a rare sound attested in only 80 languages of the world. Out of the 60 or so words that contain this consonant, 95% of them are [[Ideophone|ideophones]], words which embody the senses of their meaning. Near-minimal pairs between the labiodental flap and the labiodental fricative {{IPAslink|v}} exist: /vìw/ 'hearing something pass by' and /ⱱīw/ 'see something pass quickly'.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Pearce |first=Mary |date=2011 |title=Kera |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0025100311000168/type/journal_article |journal=Journal of the International Phonetic Association |language=en |volume=41 |issue=2 |pages=249–258 |doi=10.1017/S0025100311000168 |issn=0025-1003|doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== Vowels ===
Kera has six [[Phoneme|contrastive]] vowels. In [[closed syllables]], the mid and low vowels will undergo [[Raising (sound change)|raising]]. Kera also has phonemic [[Tone (linguistics)|tones]], whereby a change in pitch alone may differentiate words.<ref name=":0" />

==== Harmony ====
Kera has several types [[vowel harmony]]:

# High vowels in both the [[Root (linguistics)|root]] and [[suffix]] will spread and replace other vowels within the word in both directions. This is notable, as it is rare for languages to have high vowels be the dominant ones in vowel harmony systems.<ref name=":0" /> 
# Vowels in suffixes force the central vowel of the root to have the same degree of [[Vowel backness|frontness]] and [[Roundedness|rounding]].<ref name=":0" /> 
# There are several contexts which cause total harmony within the root (i.e. the vowel is wholly copied). These contexts include: word-final consonant-vowel syllables, the historical affixes -a and -a, and the [[Epenthesis|epenthetic]] vowel -i following [[Obstruent|obstruents]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Phonotactics ===

==== Clusters ====
Kera allows almost all consonants to appear at the end of a syllable in word-medial position. However, at the end of a word as a whole, only the [[Sonorant|sonorants]] /l, w, j/ can occur. When a non-sonorant sound occurs at the end of a word, the vowel [i] is added at the end to avoid breaking this rule.<ref name=":0" />

Kera's [[Syllable|syllables]] are relatively simple. It allows for a consonant to be followed by a long or short vowel and may take an extra [[Coda (linguistics)|coda]] consonant at the end. The initial consonant is optional in all cases. Additionally, there are several phonological rules at play that prevent consonant-vowel-consonant-vowel sequences from being possible. For example, the hypothetical words *[nèlɛ̀] and *[fɛ́lɛ] are phonotactically impossible in Kera. To prevent these sequences from occurring, Kera will either [[Vowel length|lengthen]] the final vowel [nèlɛ̀'''ɛ'''], or [[Elision|remove]] the final vowel [fɛ́l].<ref name=":0" />

== Grammar ==
Kera is a [[subject–verb–object]] language, using [[preposition]]s. It uses exclusively borderline [[declension|case-marking]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}
